findings.detail: The reader row is labelled `_held_worktree_rows.replace`. `git grep _held_worktree_rows a346fba4aa -- reckon/crew/obligations.py` returns nothing, and the row's own first cited line, obligations.py:2723, sits inside `_ledger_read_root` (def at :2709). The line citation itself is right - it reads `ledger.ledger_path(project, None)` and :2990 reads `ledger.ledger_path(project, root)` - so the map's substantive fact holds, but a reader acting on the function column cannot locate the caller from it.
findings.disposition_suggestion: folded: repair the function cell to `_ledger_read_root / _held_worktree_rows` at the same lines.
findings.summary: the obligations row's function label names no symbol in its module

findings.detail: The row is labelled `mutate (_wait_refusal_classes). The module is reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py, where neither name is a top-level def (`mutate` is a nested function repeated at :271, :288 and :320, and `_wait_refusal_classes` is defined at reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py:184). The cited lines :866, :880, and :2623 do read `ledger_module.run_path(...).is_file()`, so the row's read/write and via facts are correct and only the label is wrong.
findings.disposition_suggestion: folded reference to the enclosing defs at the cited lines.
findings.summary: the recovery_watch row's function label names a def that lives in a different module

findings.detail: reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py:1435 calls ledger.ledger_path(project, root) in the refusal message for `--repairs`. It is a production reference to the committed ledger path that no row names and the exclusion paragraph at :163-168 does not quote, while four other exclusions (mcp.py:2826, native_agent_guard.py:80, recovery_review_acceptance.py:758/:970, fleet_migrate.py:407) are. The read behind the message goes through open_run_index.row_for_run, so nothing breaks at cutover; only the path printed in the refusal would name a file git no longer tracks. The census's own population table calls reckon/ 'every live reader and writer', which is what makes an unlisted, unexcluded reference a defect rather than an unspecified exclusion.
findings.disposition_suggestion: folded: add the row or quote the exclusion.
findings.summary: one production ledger_path reference is neither mapped nor excluded

findings.detail: Line 50 says 'Three commit paths stage ledger files today'; line 107 says 'four commit paths will each be staging a path git no longer tracks'; line 247 says 'The four commit paths above start failing'. The writer table names exactly three distinct helpers - ledger.py:3118 `_commit_state_write`, ledger.py:3641 `_commit_run_split`, and promotion_scope.py:2508 `_commit_landing_writes` - and every 'yes' row routes through one of them. A coercing reader sizing section 6's work from this fragment gets two different populations.
findings.disposition_suggestion: folded: state one number and make lines 107 and 247 agree with it.
findings.summary: the count of commit paths disagrees with itself three vs four

findings.detail: The artifacts line records '17 writer rows, 30 reader rows'. The committed fragment's writer table holds 16 `<tr>` rows and its reader table 33. The manifest is what a coordinator reads without opening the fragment, so the population it advertises is wrong in both directions.
findings.disposition_suggestion: folded: correct the artifacts line to 16 and 33.
findings.summary: the manifest's row tallies disagree with the fragment's own tables

justifications.durability: the node ships no test file, so nothing in the suite fails if the census regresses; its guards are the gate's structural, id-prefix and grep-discrimination checks at gate-ledger-leaves-git-map.sh:57-95, which are genuinely falsified - the log shows the structure guard firing on a deleted </tr> and the id guard reporting one on a rewritten prefix - but that gate lives in the run directory and no repository test re-runs it.
justifications.evidence: the gate at logs/gate-ledger-leaves-git-map.sh:11-40 recomputes every population figure from the base blob and its log records EXIT=0, but it prints the numbers rather than asserting them against the fragment's own table values, so the match rests on an eyeball comparison; I closed that gap independently and every figure and citation matched.
justifications.fit: the fragment follows the evidence-fragment convention with node-prefixed ids at ledger-leaves-git-map-s20-writable.html:1, :23 and :55, is a bare section the composer accepts, and introduces no plan or ticket labels; the function-column inconsistency at :140 is a fit defect rather than a naming one.
justifications.goal_fidelity: docs/evidence/fragments/history-persists-as-detail-washes-out/ledger-leaves-git-map-s20-writable.html:55-161 delivers the module/read-write/commit table the section asks for, but three of its locator cells are wrong or incomplete (:140, :144, and the unlisted reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py:1435), which costs a reader a grep each time.
justifications.reuse: the census reuses git grep and git ls-tree rather than a bespoke parser and the split reuses the plan's own seven-section vocabulary; a search of reckon/ for an existing ledger-reader inventory found none, so nothing is duplicated.
justifications.scope_discipline: the commit changes one file, docs/evidence/fragments/history-persists-as-detail-washes-out/ledger-leaves-git-map-s20-writable.html, which is the first of the two declared write paths, and adds nothing the goal does not imply.

verdicts: VERDICT goal: the goal is to map every ledger reader and writer that must leave git and propose the untracking's split; the fragment at docs/evidence/fragments/history-persists-as-detail-washes-out/ledger-leaves-git-map-s20-writable.html:48-161 carries 16 writer rows and 33 reader rows at file:line, plus five migration steps (:208-237) and seven proposed sections each with a done-when (:252-310), which is the plan section's deliverable.

VERDICT done_when: the done-when asks for a git grep census at the base revision over every tracked path with tests in a separate group, a positive control naming reckon/ledger.py's writer, and each caller cited from the base blob; the worker's gate (logs/gate-ledger-leaves-git-map.sh sections 1-3) measures exactly those and its log records EXIT=0, and I reproduced every quoted population figure and about fifty citations independently against a346fba4aa.

VERDICT write_paths: the declared paths are the fragment html and a figure directory; the diff touches only the fragment, and no figure was written - permitted, since the done-when names no figure and the fragment explains at :326-328 why its two relationships are tables.

VERDICT manifest: read; it records commits 1ebacb850e, the gate command, the gate log and a positive-control log, states the gate exit 0, and flags in evidence_inputs that the done-when's fragment name omits the node suffix its own write grant carries; its artifacts line misstates the table populations (see FINDING at manifest.md:45).
VERDICT diff: read the single commit 1ebacb850e against base a346fba4aa; it adds 329 lines to one file, changes no product code, and its subject and body state what landed and why.

VERDICT call_sites: three production call sites reach a fragment under docs/evidence/fragments/ - the composer at reckon/evidence.py:compose_landed_record (which resolves a fragment as <node>.html at :744 and appends its body via _fragment_body_bytes at :640), the classifier reckon/resources.py:_is_evidence_fragment at :244, and the serving path in reckon/serve.py; the bare-<section> form the fragment uses is the explicitly supported 'bare fragment anchor' case at evidence.py:656.
